title: Cazoo Cars for Sale
meta_title: Cazoo Cars for Sale: What the Brand Is Now (2026)
meta_description: Cazoo no longer sells or delivers cars. What the 2026 marketplace actually is, who protects your purchase, and how its 300,000 listings work.
intro:
"Cazoo does not deliver or even sell cars." That sentence appears on Cazoo's own about page, and it is the quickest route to understanding why almost everything written about this brand before 2025 is now a poor guide to what you will find.

The Cazoo that sponsored football shirts bought cars outright, reconditioned them in its own centres, delivered them on a transporter and offered a seven-day money-back guarantee. That operation consumed more than £400m and went into administration in early 2024. MOTORS bought the brand name out of the wreckage in June 2024 for around £5m. It bought the name, not the machine.

What wears the badge in 2026 is a classified marketplace: 300,000+ cars listed monthly from 6,000+ dealers, relaunched in April 2025 with over 250,000 listings, app first and website second. The legal entity is Motors.co.uk Limited, trading as Cazoo, and since 27 May 2026 it is the group's only consumer-facing brand.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying from in 2026
sections.html:
Every car on Cazoo belongs to a dealer. Cazoo takes no ownership, holds no stock, runs no preparation centre and arranges no delivery. Your contract of sale is with the franchised or independent retailer whose forecourt the car sits on.

That distinction has practical consequences. The seven-day returns promise, the standardised 90-point check and the fixed no-haggle pricing that defined old Cazoo are gone with the company that offered them. Warranty length, part-exchange terms, admin fees and whether the price is negotiable are now set individually by whichever of the 6,000+ dealers you contact — and they vary enormously between them.

Cazoo's own research puts spontaneous brand awareness among UK used-car buyers at roughly 60%, which CEO Barry Judge has used to claim second place behind Auto Trader. That awareness is inherited from the failed retailer, and it is worth being blunt: a large share of the people who recognise the name recognise it for services the current business does not provide.

sections.heading: 300,000 listings a month, and where they come from
sections.html:
The monthly listing figure is genuine scale — comfortably the second-largest pool advertised by any provider in this comparison, behind Auto Trader's 457,000 average live cars. Depth of stock is the real argument for using Cazoo.

Search, saved searches and enquiries cost the buyer nothing. The revenue comes from dealers, who pay for placement across the group's advertising network rather than for a single site.

The relaunch sequence matters if you are choosing a device. Cazoo rebuilt as an app first in April 2025, with the website following. If a feature seems missing on desktop, checking the app before concluding it does not exist is usually worth the two minutes.

sections.heading: Finance is brokered to CarMoney, not funded by Cazoo
sections.html:
Cazoo acts as a credit broker, not a lender. Finance enquiries are passed to a third-party lender, CarMoney Limited. Cazoo does not underwrite, does not hold the agreement and is not the party you would complain to about the loan.

Two things follow for anyone comparing monthly payments:

  • The APR you are quoted is CarMoney's, subject to its own credit assessment and pricing — check current rates with the provider before you commit, as no headline rate is published on a fixed basis.
  • Dealer-arranged finance on the same car may come from a different lender entirely. Getting both quotes on the same vehicle is the only reliable way to see which is cheaper.

Broker commission arrangements should be disclosed to you in writing before you sign. If they are not, ask.

sections.heading: The protection gap most buyers do not spot
sections.html:
When a marketplace introduces you to a dealer, the Consumer Rights Act protections you rely on run against that dealer, not the marketplace. A car sold by a VAT-registered trader must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described, and you have short-term rejection rights if it is not — but you exercise those against the seller.

Cazoo is not a party to your purchase and cannot refund you. If the selling dealer folds, ceases trading or simply refuses to engage, the marketplace has no fund standing behind the transaction. This is normal for classified sites and identical at Auto Trader, but it is a genuine step down from the old Cazoo model that many returning users still assume is in place.

Practical mitigations: pay any deposit by credit card so Section 75 may apply, check the dealer's own returns and warranty terms in writing before travelling, and take an independent inspection on anything expensive.

sections.heading: The same car, five times, on five websites
sections.html:
Cazoo sits inside an advertising network in which one dealer invoice buys placement across MOTORS, eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers. Dealers like it because the average car buyer visits 4.2 websites during a search.

The consequence for you is duplication. A car you spot on Parkers, a car you spot on Gumtree and a car you spot on Cazoo may be one physical vehicle advertised three times. Cross-checking those sites will not widen your choice the way cross-checking Cazoo against Auto Trader or Carwow will, because those two are genuinely separate inventory pools.

pros: 300,000+ cars listed monthly from 6,000+ dealers — the second-deepest pool among the sites compared here
Completely free for buyers to search, save and enquire
Relaunched app is the primary product and is genuinely well built for phone-first searching
Very high name recognition (~60% spontaneous) means most dealers are already on it
Backed by an established owner, O3 Industries / Novum Capital, rather than venture funding that needs constant replenishment
cons: The brand no longer offers home delivery, a money-back guarantee or its own reconditioning — returning users regularly expect all three
Cazoo is not a party to your purchase, so all consumer redress sits with the individual dealer
Finance is brokered to CarMoney Limited, so rates and decisions are outside Cazoo's control and are not published as headline figures
Listings duplicate across Gumtree, eBay and Parkers, which inflates the apparent size of the market you are searching
Buying standards vary dealer by dealer — no group-wide inspection, warranty or pricing policy replaces the old retail model
verdict: Cazoo suits a buyer who wants a big, free, phone-friendly classified search and is comfortable doing their own diligence on the selling dealer — checking its warranty terms, its trading history and the car itself. It is a reasonable second search to run alongside Auto Trader. It does not suit anyone who came here because they remember Cazoo delivering a checked car to the door with a no-quibble return window; that business closed in 2024 and nothing on the current site replaces it. Anyone who wants the marketplace itself to stand behind the transaction should buy from a franchised dealer's own approved-used programme instead, where the manufacturer's scheme provides the guarantee.

faqs.q: Does Cazoo still deliver cars to my door?
faqs.a: No. Home delivery ended when the original Cazoo retail business went into administration in early 2024. The current site states plainly that Cazoo does not deliver or sell cars — it introduces you to a dealer, and any delivery arrangement is negotiated with that dealer directly.

faqs.q: Is the seven-day money-back guarantee still available?
faqs.a: No. That guarantee belonged to the old retail operation and did not transfer with the brand name. Some individual dealers offer their own returns policies, but there is no group-wide equivalent, so you need to check the terms in writing before you buy.

faqs.q: Who lends the money if I take finance through Cazoo?
faqs.a: Cazoo is a credit broker and refers customers to CarMoney Limited, a third-party lender. The rate and the decision are CarMoney's, not Cazoo's. Check current rates with the provider and compare them against the dealer's own finance quote on the same car.

faqs.q: Why do I keep seeing the same cars on Gumtree and Parkers?
faqs.a: Because they are the same stock. One dealer advertising package covers MOTORS, eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers, so a single vehicle appears on all of them. To genuinely widen your search, compare against Auto Trader or Carwow, which run separate inventory.

faqs.q: Is Motors.co.uk the same company as Cazoo?
faqs.a: Yes. Motors.co.uk Limited bought the Cazoo brand in 2024 and retired its own Motors brand on 27 May 2026. motors.co.uk now redirects to cazoo.co.uk.

title: Carwow Cars for Sale
meta_title: Carwow Cars for Sale: Free to Sell, Dealers Bid
meta_description: Carwow charges nothing to sell your car: 6,000+ dealers bid, you set the reserve, sale in 24 hours. What it won't accept and where it falls short.
intro:
Nothing. That is the fee Carwow charges a private seller — and the company is unusually direct about naming who it thinks does charge, stating on its own selling page that "unlike other sites like WeBuyAnyCar and Motorway, it's always completely free to sell your car with Carwow. No hidden costs, no admin fees, nothing."

The model behind that claim is an auction rather than a classified advert. You submit the car, it goes into a daily sale, and 6,000+ dealers bid against each other for it. You set the reserve. If a bid clears it, the winning dealer arranges collection and pays — potentially the same day. A car can go from listed to sold in 24 hours.

Since launching car selling in 2021, Carwow says it has facilitated 122,000+ used car sales worth £1.6bn, and it has helped more than 2.5m people buy or sell since 2011. Roughly one in ten new cars registered privately in the UK is bought through the platform.

sections.heading: Why the seller pays nothing, and who does
sections.html:
The money comes from the dealer side. Winning bidders pay Carwow for access to the auction and the vehicle, which means the seller's headline price is the price. There is no deduction on collection, no listing fee and no admin charge subtracted from the transfer.

Compare that structurally with a fixed-price instant buyer, where the quoted figure is frequently revised downward at inspection, and with a classified advert, where you pay upfront for exposure regardless of whether the car sells. Carwow's arrangement removes both risks for the seller and shifts the commercial pressure onto the dealers competing for stock.

The trade-off is control. In a private classified sale you negotiate directly and can hold out indefinitely. In an auction you find out what the trade will pay this week — a number that reflects dealer margins, not private-buyer sentiment, and one that will usually sit below what a patient private sale achieves.

sections.heading: Setting a reserve and the 24-hour clock
sections.html:
The reserve is yours to set, and it is the single most important decision in the process. Set it too high and the auction closes without a sale; set it too low and you are contractually exposed to a bid you regret.

The mechanics worth knowing before you start:

  • Bidding runs as a daily auction, so you are not waiting weeks for a result.
  • A sale can complete in as little as 24 hours from listing.
  • If the car does not sell first time, Carwow offers a two-day extension rather than making you relist from scratch.
  • The winning dealer collects the car, and same-day payment is available.

Photographs and an honest description do most of the work on price here. Dealers are bidding from your listing rather than a physical inspection, and a bid that has to be revised downwards when the car is collected is a wasted day for everyone.

sections.heading: Cars Carwow will not take
sections.html:
The exclusions are narrow but absolute. Carwow does not accept insurance write-offs, and it does not accept former service vehicles such as ambulances and taxis.

What is notable is what is not excluded. Carwow states no minimum or maximum value, no age cap and no mileage limit. A high-mileage twelve-year-old hatchback and a nearly new performance car are both eligible, which is a wider gate than several rivals apply.

If your car has a Category S or N marker, this is not the route. A specialist salvage-aware buyer or a private sale with full disclosure will serve you better, and attempting to conceal the marker would unwind the sale in any case.

sections.heading: Auto Express, evo and the media machine behind the site
sections.html:
In February 2024 Carwow acquired Autovia, bringing Auto Express, Carbuyer, evo, DrivingElectric and the Driver Power owner satisfaction survey under the same roof. Those titles reach around 15m car owners a month, on top of Carwow's own 2.5m monthly users and a YouTube channel that drew 1.1bn views in 2023.

No other provider in this comparison owns both a marketplace and the enthusiast magazines that review the cars sold on it. For a buyer, it means the review, the reliability survey data and the transaction live in one ecosystem. It is also worth naming the tension: a business that earns from dealer transactions also publishes the editorial verdicts, and readers should weigh recommendations with that in mind.

One figure to treat carefully — the sell-my-car page cites 6,000+ bidding dealers, while the February 2024 Autovia announcement referenced 4,500+ dealer partners. Both are Carwow's own numbers from different dates; the older figure is the one to quote if you need a dated source.

sections.heading: The gap in the offering: used-car classified depth
sections.html:
Carwow's centre of gravity is new-car discounting and car selling. It does not publish a used-car listing count that stands comparison with Auto Trader's 457,000 average live cars or Cazoo's 300,000 listed monthly.

If you are hunting for a specific used car — a particular trim, colour and gearbox within forty miles — Carwow is the wrong first stop. Its strength is in the other direction of travel: getting dealers to compete for your business, whether that means bidding for the car you are disposing of or discounting the new one you are ordering.

pros: Genuinely free for the seller — no listing fee, no admin fee, nothing deducted at collection
6,000+ dealers bidding competitively rather than one buyer making a take-it-or-leave-it offer
You set the reserve, so there is a floor you control
Sale possible within 24 hours, with a two-day extension if the first auction fails
Dealer collects the car and same-day payment is available
No stated minimum or maximum value, age or mileage limit
Owns Auto Express, Carbuyer, evo, DrivingElectric and the Driver Power survey — research and transaction in one place
Strong track record: 122,000+ used car sales worth £1.6bn since 2021
cons: Trade bids will generally come in below a patient private sale — you are selling to the motor trade, not to an end user
Thin as a used-car search destination; no published listing count comparable to Auto Trader or Cazoo
Insurance write-offs and ex-service vehicles such as taxis and ambulances are refused outright
Dealer-count figures differ between Carwow's own sources (6,000+ on the selling page, 4,500+ in the Feb 2024 release)
Owning the magazines that review the cars it profits from selling creates an editorial conflict worth keeping in view
An auction result is a market test, not a guaranteed sale — the car may not clear your reserve at all
verdict: Carwow is the strongest option on this list if you are selling a car and want competitive bidding without paying a penny for it, or if you are buying a new car and want dealers to compete on discount. The combination of a seller-set reserve, free entry, 24-hour turnaround and doorstep collection is hard to beat for anyone who values speed and certainty over squeezing out the last few hundred pounds. It is the wrong choice if you are searching for a specific used car, where Auto Trader's 457,000 live listings make it a far more productive place to start. It is also no use at all if your car is a Category S or N write-off, an ex-taxi or an ex-ambulance, or if you have the patience and the time to sell privately and want the higher price that usually brings.

faqs.q: Is selling through Carwow really free?
faqs.a: Yes for the private seller. Carwow states there are no hidden costs and no admin fees, and it earns from the dealer who wins the auction rather than from you. The figure you agree is the figure you receive.

faqs.q: What happens if nobody bids above my reserve?
faqs.a: The car does not sell, and Carwow offers a two-day extension to give more dealers a chance to bid. If it still fails to clear, the usual fix is to review the reserve against the bids you did receive — those bids are the market's answer on what the trade will pay.

faqs.q: Will Carwow accept a Category S or Category N car?
faqs.a: No. Insurance write-offs are excluded, as are former service vehicles such as ambulances and taxis. A write-off is better sold privately with full disclosure or through a salvage-aware specialist.

faqs.q: Can I use Carwow to search for a used car?
faqs.a: You can, but it is not where Carwow is strong. It publishes no used-car listing count comparable to Auto Trader's 457,000 average live cars, and its focus is new-car discounting and selling. Start a used search elsewhere and use Carwow for the disposal side.

faqs.q: How quickly will I get paid?
faqs.a: The winning dealer collects the car and same-day payment is available, with the whole process capable of completing within 24 hours of listing. Confirm the payment method and timing with the buying dealer before you hand over the keys.

title: Parkers Cars for Sale
meta_title: Parkers Cars for Sale: Reviews First, Stock Borrowed
meta_description: Parkers writes the reviews and valuations but borrows its classified stock. Who supplies the listings now, what changed in 2024, and how to use it.
intro:
Two different businesses share the Parkers domain, and telling them apart is the whole point of this page. One is a five-decade-old car research publisher owned by Bauer Media — valuations, expert reviews, running costs, specification data. The other is a classified marketplace bolted onto it, and Parkers does not own a single car in it.

Since 28 August 2024, the cars-for-sale inventory on Parkers has been supplied by the MOTORS/Cazoo network. Before that, from September 2022, it came from heycar, a partnership that gave Parkers access to 80,000 used car ads. Two suppliers in four years, neither of them Parkers.

That inversion — research first, stock second — is the opposite of how Auto Trader and Cazoo are built, and it changes how you should use the site. Parkers is where you work out what a car is worth and whether it is any good. It is not where the widest search happens.

sections.heading: Fifty years of guides, four years of borrowed listings
sections.html:
Parkers began life as Parker's Car Guides and, in the words of its own Digital Operations Director, has been "helping consumers research and buy used cars for over 50 years". The printed price guide was the reference point for a generation of British buyers arguing over a forecourt price.

That heritage is real and it is the asset. What it does not include is a dealer sales force, a stock feed or a network of forecourt relationships. Bauer Media publishes; it does not run a marketplace. Every classified advert you see on Parkers arrived through a commercial agreement with a company that does.

sections.heading: Valuations and running costs — the actual reason to be here
sections.html:
The Parkers valuation is the tool most people come for, and it does something none of the pure marketplaces do: it gives you an independent reference figure to hold a dealer's asking price against.

Alongside it sit expert reviews, spec-by-spec trim data and running-cost breakdowns covering fuel, insurance groups, road tax bands and expected servicing. For anyone deciding which car rather than which advert, that combination is more useful than another 100,000 listings.

Research on Parkers is free to use. What is not verified is Parkers' FCA credit-broker permissions and whether commission arrangements on any finance or leasing products it promotes are disclosed on the page — check the provider's own regulatory disclosures before taking a finance quote through the site, and treat any monthly figure as indicative until confirmed by the actual lender.

sections.heading: The supplier has changed twice since 2022
sections.html:
This is the structural weakness, and it is not a hypothetical one:

  • September 2022 — heycar partnership announced, giving Parkers access to 80,000 used car ads.
  • 28 August 2024 — that arrangement gave way to the MOTORS/Cazoo network.

Listing depth, geographic coverage, photo quality and the mix of franchised versus independent dealers on Parkers are all determined by whoever holds the contract at the time. If the supplier changes again, the search results change with it, and Parkers has no ability to backfill from its own stock because it has none.

The current live listing count on parkers.co.uk is not verified — it is not published as a headline figure and should be checked on the site itself before you assume the pool is comparable to Auto Trader's 457,000 average live cars.

sections.heading: You are searching Cazoo's stock without leaving Parkers
sections.html:
The MOTORS/Cazoo network sells dealers one invoice covering placement across MOTORS, eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers. The pitch to dealers rests on the average car buyer visiting 4.2 websites during a search.

Which means a car you find on Parkers is very likely the same physical vehicle listed on Cazoo and Gumtree. Searching all three is repetition dressed as diligence. If you want a genuinely wider net, the second search should be Auto Trader, which operates an entirely separate inventory pool.

The other consequence: the buyer protections attached to any purchase come from the selling dealer. Parkers introduces you to an advert it did not create, for a car it does not hold, sold by a dealer it has no contract with. It cannot refund you, mediate a dispute or stand behind the description.

sections.heading: A sensible order of operations
sections.html:
The way to get value out of Parkers is to use it for what it owns and go elsewhere for what it borrows:

  • Shortlist models using the reviews, spec tables and running-cost data.
  • Pull a valuation for the exact year, trim and mileage you are targeting, and write the number down.
  • Run the actual search on Auto Trader for breadth, and on Cazoo if you want the network stock in its native home.
  • Come back to the Parkers valuation when you negotiate.

Used that way it is a genuinely strong free resource. Used as a primary marketplace, it is a smaller window onto somebody else's inventory.

pros: Over 50 years of car guide heritage under Bauer Media ownership — the valuations are a recognised independent reference point
Free expert reviews, trim-level spec data and running-cost breakdowns covering fuel, insurance groups and tax bands
Genuinely useful for deciding which car to buy, which pure marketplaces handle poorly
Research and classifieds in one place, so you can move from a review to an advert without changing site
No cost to use any of the research tools
cons: Owns none of its classified stock — every listing is syndicated from a third party
The supplier has changed twice since 2022 (heycar in 2022, MOTORS/Cazoo from August 2024), so search depth is outside Parkers' control
Listings duplicate Cazoo and Gumtree, so searching Parkers as well adds little to your options
Current live listing count is not published — do not assume it matches Auto Trader's 457,000 average live cars
Parkers' FCA credit-broker permissions and finance commission disclosures are unverified — check directly before taking any quote
No consumer redress from Parkers itself; all rights run against the selling dealer
verdict: Parkers is the best free research tool in this comparison and the weakest marketplace in it. Use it if you are still deciding which car to buy, want a defensible valuation to take into a negotiation, or need running costs and trim differences laid out clearly — that is work Auto Trader, Cazoo and Carwow all do less well. Do not use it as your main search. Its stock is a borrowed feed from the Cazoo network, it duplicates what you would see on Cazoo and Gumtree, and its depth can change whenever the supply contract does. Buyers who want the widest possible choice should search Auto Trader; sellers should ignore Parkers entirely and go to Carwow, which costs nothing and puts thousands of dealers in competition for the car.

faqs.q: Does Parkers sell cars itself?
faqs.a: No. Parkers is a Bauer Media publisher. Its cars-for-sale section displays adverts supplied by a partner network — currently MOTORS/Cazoo — and every sale is between you and the dealer who placed the advert.

faqs.q: Where do Parkers' listings come from?
faqs.a: Since 28 August 2024 they come from the MOTORS/Cazoo network. From September 2022 until then they came from heycar, a partnership that provided access to 80,000 used car ads. Parkers has no stock of its own to fall back on.

faqs.q: How accurate is a Parkers valuation?
faqs.a: It is a guide figure based on the year, trim, mileage and condition you enter, not a binding offer. Treat it as a reference point to test an asking price against, and expect trade offers to sit below it and private sale prices to sit above it.

faqs.q: Is it worth searching Parkers as well as Cazoo?
faqs.a: Rarely. Both draw on the same network stock, so you will see many of the same cars twice. Auto Trader runs a separate inventory pool, which makes it the more productive second search.

faqs.q: Can Parkers help if a car I bought turns out to be faulty?
faqs.a: No. Your rights under the Consumer Rights Act run against the dealer who sold you the car. Parkers did not own the vehicle, did not write the advert and is not a party to the contract.

title: Auto Trader Cars for Sale
meta_title: Auto Trader Cars for Sale: 457,000 Live Listings
meta_description: 457,000 cars and 83.3m monthly visits — set against a £2,994 monthly dealer fee rising faster than its audience. A numbers-first Auto Trader review.
intro:
457,000 cars. 83.3 million visits a month. Over 75% of all time spent on UK automotive marketplaces. Auto Trader is the only provider in this comparison that is a listed public company, which means its claims are audited rather than asserted — and the figures above come from its H1 FY2026 results, covering the six months to 30 September 2025 and announced on 6 November 2025.

For a buyer, that scale settles the question of where to start a search. No other UK site puts that many cars in front of you, and the gap over the second-placed pool is roughly 150,000 vehicles.

For a dealer, the same results contain the sharpest criticism anyone makes of the business: average revenue per retailer reached £2,994 a month, up £142 or 5%, while visits grew 1% and total minutes on site were flat. Cost per forecourt is climbing considerably faster than the audience being delivered — and that is Auto Trader's own arithmetic, not a rival's.

sections.heading: The numbers behind the market position
sections.html:
H1 FY2026, six months to 30 September 2025:

  • Live car stock: 457,000 average, up 2%
  • Retailer forecourts: 14,080 average, up 1%
  • Cross-platform visits: 83.3m a month, up 1%
  • Cross-platform minutes: 559m a month, flat
  • Share of time on UK auto marketplaces: over 75%
  • Group revenue: £317.7m, up 5% — of which the Auto Trader segment is £296.3m, up 5%
  • Group operating profit: £200.1m, up 6%
  • Basic EPS: 17.26p, up 11%

The 75% share-of-time figure is the one that matters most to a buyer. It means that for every four minutes British car shoppers spend on a marketplace, three of them are on Auto Trader — which is why almost every dealer with stock to shift advertises here, whatever they think of the price.

sections.heading: £2,994 a month, and who ends up paying it
sections.html:
Auto Trader charges dealers, not buyers. Searching, saving and enquiring cost you nothing. The £2,994 monthly ARPR is what the average forecourt pays for the privilege of being seen, across 14,080 forecourts.

That cost is not invisible to you. Advertising is a fixed overhead a dealer has to recover across the cars it sells, and a site that takes just under £3,000 a month from a small independent shifting fifteen cars is taking roughly £200 out of each of them. Pricing on any marketplace reflects the cost of being on it.

The direction of travel is what dealers object to. ARPR rose 5% year on year; visits rose 1%; minutes did not move. More money for the same eyeballs is a defensible complaint, and it is the single most credible negative anyone can raise about the business because it comes straight out of the interim results.

Individual dealer package pricing is negotiated and not published as a rate card — dealers should get current pricing direct from Auto Trader rather than relying on the sector average.

sections.heading: Deal Builder and Co-Driver: tools nobody else in this list has
sections.html:
Two products separate Auto Trader from every other provider here.

Deal Builder handles part-exchange valuation and vehicle reservation online, so a buyer can lock a car and settle the outline of the deal before travelling. It is live with 4,000+ retailers — a meaningful share of the 14,080 forecourts, but not all of them, so check whether the specific dealer supports it before assuming you can reserve.

Co-Driver is a set of AI listing tools used by 10,000+ customers, credited with creating 1 million improved listings. From the buyer's side this shows up as more complete, more consistently written adverts with fewer of the three-line descriptions that make comparison impossible.

Neither Cazoo, Parkers nor Carwow offers an equivalent to either product.

sections.heading: What the flat audience means for you
sections.html:
An audience that is not growing is not the same as an audience that is shrinking, and 83.3m visits a month against 559m minutes still represents dominance no rival is close to. What it does mean is that Auto Trader's growth now comes from charging its existing dealers more rather than from bringing more buyers in.

Auto Trader has said that two of every three of its customers' used car sales are generated through its marketplace — though that claim dates from a 2022 press release and should be treated as historical rather than current.

The practical risk to a buyer is limited. The practical risk to a small independent dealer is real: an advertising cost rising at 5% a year against flat delivered traffic squeezes margin, and squeezed margin tends to reappear as tighter part-exchange offers and less room on price.

sections.heading: Where Auto Trader still leaves gaps
sections.html:
Scale does not solve everything:

  • Selling privately is not free here. If your priority is disposing of a car at no cost, Carwow charges the seller nothing and puts 6,000+ dealers into competition for it.
  • Research depth is not the strength. Parkers' valuations, running-cost tables and long-form reviews remain the better tool for deciding which model to buy.
  • No consumer redress from the platform. As with every classified site here, your Consumer Rights Act protections run against the selling dealer, not Auto Trader. Pay deposits by credit card so Section 75 may apply.
  • Volume cuts both ways. 457,000 cars is a lot to filter, and the sheer number of near-identical results can make a decision harder rather than easier.

pros: 457,000 average live cars — by a wide margin the deepest used-car pool in the UK
Over 75% of all time spent on UK automotive marketplaces happens here
83.3m visits a month means virtually every dealer with stock advertises on it
Deal Builder lets you value a part-exchange and reserve a car online at 4,000+ retailers
Co-Driver AI tools have improved 1 million listings, producing fuller and more comparable adverts
Free for buyers to search, save and enquire
Audited public-company figures rather than self-reported marketing claims
cons: Dealer cost of £2,994 per forecourt per month is rising 5% a year against visits up just 1% and minutes flat
That advertising overhead is recovered through car prices and tighter part-exchange offers
Not free for private sellers — Carwow costs nothing and runs a competitive auction
Weaker than Parkers for valuations, running costs and model research
Deal Builder covers 4,000+ of 14,080 forecourts, so online reservation is not available everywhere
No protection from the platform itself — all redress is against the selling dealer
The 'two in three used car sales' claim dates from 2022 and should not be read as current
verdict: Start here if you are buying a used car and want the widest possible choice — 457,000 live listings and three-quarters of all UK marketplace attention make Auto Trader the default first search, and Deal Builder is the only tool in this comparison that lets you value a part-exchange and reserve a car before you set off. It suits buyers hunting a specific trim, colour or gearbox within a defined radius, where volume genuinely helps. It is the wrong choice for a private seller, who should use Carwow and pay nothing, and it is the wrong place to research which car to buy, where Parkers' valuations and running-cost data are stronger. Small independent dealers weighing a package should look hard at the £2,994 sector average rising 5% against a flat audience, and negotiate on the basis of leads delivered rather than headline reach.

faqs.q: How many cars are on Auto Trader?
faqs.a: Live car stock averaged 457,000 in the six months to 30 September 2025, up 2% year on year, across an average of 14,080 retailer forecourts. That is roughly 150,000 more than the next-largest pool in this comparison.

faqs.q: What do dealers pay to advertise on Auto Trader?
faqs.a: Average revenue per retailer was £2,994 a month in H1 FY2026, up £142 or 5%. Individual packages are negotiated and no public rate card exists, so dealers should get current pricing direct from Auto Trader rather than budgeting from the sector average.

faqs.q: Is Auto Trader getting more expensive without delivering more buyers?
faqs.a: On its own figures, yes in relative terms. ARPR rose 5% while cross-platform visits rose 1% and total minutes were flat. Auto Trader still holds over 75% of time spent on UK auto marketplaces, so the audience is dominant — it is simply not growing at the rate the price is.

faqs.q: What is Deal Builder and can I use it on any car?
faqs.a: Deal Builder handles online part-exchange valuation and vehicle reservation so you can secure a car before visiting. It is live with 4,000+ retailers out of around 14,080 forecourts, so check the individual listing rather than assuming it is available.

faqs.q: Does Auto Trader protect me if the car is faulty?
faqs.a: No. Your rights under the Consumer Rights Act run against the dealer who sold you the car. Auto Trader hosts the advert but is not a party to the sale. Paying a deposit by credit card may give you additional protection under Section 75.

title: Motors.co.uk Cars for Sale
meta_title: Motors.co.uk Cars for Sale: Now Redirects to Cazoo
meta_description: Motors.co.uk was retired on 27 May 2026 and now redirects to Cazoo. What happened to the brand, what survived it, and where your saved searches went.
intro:
Type motors.co.uk/used-cars into a browser today and you do not arrive at Motors. You get an HTTP 302 redirect to cazoo.co.uk/cars. That is the whole story in one line: the Motors brand was retired on 27 May 2026, and the business now trades solely as Cazoo.

The domain has not been switched off. It is being kept alive purely as a redirect until late 2026, which means old bookmarks, old links and old search results still function — they simply land somewhere else. After that window closes, they will not.

None of this was a failure. The company doing the redirecting is the one that bought the Cazoo name out of administration in June 2024 for around £5m and then decided the acquired brand had more consumer recognition than its own. Motors.co.uk Limited still exists as the legal entity — it just trades under a different name.

sections.heading: 27 May 2026: the date the name stopped being used
sections.html:
The switch was deliberate and complete. Every consumer-facing touchpoint moved to Cazoo on that date, and the reasoning was brand equity: Cazoo's spontaneous awareness among UK used-car buyers runs at around 60%, which the company's chief executive Barry Judge has claimed makes it the second best-known used car marketplace in Britain behind Auto Trader.

Motors, despite nearly two decades of trading, never got close to that. Buying a collapsed rival's name and then adopting it is an unusual move, but on the awareness numbers it is a rational one.

Practically, this means anything you read about Motors.co.uk written before mid-2026 describes a website that no longer serves customers. There is no separate Motors inventory, no separate Motors account and no separate Motors app.

sections.heading: From DMGT start-up to buying a failed unicorn's name
sections.html:
• 2007 — founded by DMGT, the Daily Mail and General Trust.
  • 2021 — acquired by O3 Industries / Novum Capital, who remain the owners.
  • 2023 — rebranded from "Motors.co.uk" to the shorter "Motors".
  • June 2024 — buys the Cazoo brand out of administration for around £5m.
  • 28 August 2024 — announces a partnership putting its stock on Parkers.
  • April 2025 — relaunches Cazoo as a marketplace, app first, with over 250,000 listings.
  • 27 May 2026 — retires the Motors brand entirely.

The arc is worth understanding because it explains the current shape of the market. Cazoo's 300,000+ monthly listings and 6,000+ dealers are Motors' listings and Motors' dealers, wearing a name that used to belong to a company that spent £400m and folded.

sections.heading: The one asset that survived intact: the five-site network
sections.html:
Motors' genuine differentiator was never its own website traffic. It was distribution. One dealer invoice bought advertising across MOTORS, eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers — five destinations, one bill, one stock feed.

The pitch to dealers rested on a specific behavioural finding: the average car buyer visits 4.2 websites during a search. Rather than fight for the whole journey, the network aimed to be present at several points on it.

That network is untouched by the rebrand. It now sits under the Cazoo banner with one fewer destination in the list, and it remains the most distinctive thing about the group. It is also why searching Cazoo, Gumtree and Parkers as three separate exercises is largely wasted effort — you are looking at one pool three times.

Dealer pricing for the network is not published. No public rate card exists, so any dealer weighing it against Auto Trader's £2,994 monthly sector average should request current pricing directly.

sections.heading: What to do with an old bookmark, saved search or dealer account
sections.html:
For buyers:

  • Old motors.co.uk links still resolve, but only until the redirect is retired in late 2026. Update anything you rely on now.
  • Saved searches and alerts should be recreated on Cazoo. Do not assume they migrated silently.
  • The cars you were watching are almost certainly still listed — same dealers, same stock, different domain.

For dealers:

  • Your advertising contract sits with Motors.co.uk Limited, which still exists and still trades — under the Cazoo name.
  • Placement across eBay, Gumtree and Parkers continues as before.
  • Check that any of your own marketing, forecourt signage or website badges still pointing at Motors are updated before the redirect window closes.

sections.heading: Where this leaves you if you came here to search
sections.html:
There is no Motors.co.uk to review any more, so the honest recommendation is about where to go instead.

If you want the network stock in its proper home, go to Cazoo — 300,000+ listings monthly from 6,000+ dealers, free to search, with the caveat that Cazoo is a pure marketplace and all consumer protection rests with the selling dealer. If you want genuine breadth beyond that pool, Auto Trader runs entirely separate inventory at 457,000 average live cars. If you are selling rather than buying, Carwow charges the private seller nothing and runs a daily auction with 6,000+ bidding dealers.

pros: The redirect is clean and automatic — no listings or dealers were lost in the transition
The multi-site network survives intact: one dealer package still covers eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers
Stock moved to a bigger, better-recognised brand with around 60% spontaneous awareness
Motors.co.uk Limited remains the trading entity, so existing dealer contracts continue
Old links keep working during the wind-down period, giving time to update bookmarks
cons: The brand no longer exists — there is nothing left to compare on its own merits
The redirect is temporary and scheduled to end in late 2026, after which old links break
Buyers who trusted the Motors name are now transacting under a brand associated with a company that went into administration
No published dealer rate card for the network, making cost comparison against Auto Trader impossible without a direct quote
Network duplication means Cazoo, Gumtree and Parkers show substantially the same cars, so the apparent choice is smaller than it looks
verdict: There is no live Motors.co.uk to recommend or reject. The brand was retired on 27 May 2026, motors.co.uk/used-cars now returns a 302 redirect to cazoo.co.uk/cars, and the domain is being kept alive only until late 2026. Anyone who arrived here from an old bookmark should go straight to Cazoo, where the same 6,000+ dealers and 300,000+ monthly listings live, and should recreate any saved searches rather than assuming they carried over. Dealers who bought the multi-site network package still have it — coverage across eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers is unchanged — but should ask for current pricing in writing, since no rate card is public. Buyers wanting inventory outside this pool need Auto Trader, and private sellers should use Carwow, which is free.

faqs.q: Has Motors.co.uk closed down?
faqs.a: The brand has been retired, not the business. Motors.co.uk Limited still exists and still trades, but as Cazoo. The website now redirects to cazoo.co.uk, and the domain is being maintained purely for that purpose until late 2026.

faqs.q: Why did Motors take the name of a company that went bust?
faqs.a: Brand recognition. Cazoo's spontaneous awareness among UK used-car buyers runs at around 60%, which the company claims puts it second only to Auto Trader. Motors never achieved comparable recognition in nearly two decades of trading, so the acquired name was judged the more valuable asset.

faqs.q: What happened to my saved searches and alerts?
faqs.a: Recreate them on Cazoo rather than assuming they transferred. The underlying stock is the same — same dealers, same cars — but you should set up alerts fresh on the new site and update any bookmarks before the redirect is switched off.

faqs.q: Do dealers still get eBay and Gumtree placement?
faqs.a: Yes. The multi-site network is the group's most distinctive product and it survived the rebrand intact. One dealer package still covers eBay, Gumtree, Cazoo and Parkers. Pricing is not published, so request a current quote directly.

faqs.q: Where should I search now instead?
faqs.a: Cazoo holds the same inventory, at 300,000+ cars listed monthly from 6,000+ dealers. For stock outside that pool, Auto Trader is the separate and larger option at 457,000 average live cars. If you are selling rather than buying, Carwow is free for private sellers.
